description:
FILED s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5), found writing the #463 negative rows.
PRE-EXISTING (neither s446k repair fires on it).

  my @f = sort <./nope-*-xyz>;
    PPI: Word(sort) Operator(<) Operator(.) Regexp::Match(/nope-*-xyz>;)
    PCL: statement dropped -- "Handle single node of unknown type. Dump:"
    perl: an empty list (no such files)

This is docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md Â§14 + Â§14b: the term-position `<` is read as
less-than (Â§14), and the `/` that follows then starts a match which swallows
the rest of the statement (Â§14b, the cascade).  s446k's
`_repair_readline_cascade` does NOT fire because its body test is perlop's
READLINE whitelist (empty, a bareword handle, a simple scalar) and
`./nope-*-xyz` is a glob PATTERN.

Note the two existing workarounds interact here: `Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_glob_after_block`
rebuilds `< â¦ >` runs into a Readline token, and `_repair_word_match` has a
guard specifically NOT to treat the `/` inside a derailed `<op/*>` run as a
match.  Neither can reach this one, because the `/` was already consumed into
a Regexp token before either runs.

SHAPE: extend `_repair_readline_cascade`'s body test to the glob-pattern case
-- but the body is no longer a token run there (it is inside the Regexp
token's TEXT), so the repair would have to reconstruct `<` â¦ `>` from the
Regexp content up to the `>`.  Probe first how many spellings that is; the
population scan in the s446k report found ZERO sites of the readline cascade
and this one shape of the pattern cascade (`<op/*.t>` after `sort` in
t/op/readdir.t:38 is the same family and IS in the companion population).
subject: A diamond glob PATTERN containing `.` derails into a Regexp that swallows the statement -- `my @f = sort <./nope-*-xyz>;` drops whole (#479's family, one step out)
